related_questions.question: What is the new retirement law passed by Congress 2025?

text_blocks.snippet: In 2025, several changes to retirement laws were enacted, primarily stemming from the SECURE 2.0 Act. These changes include increased catch-up contribution limits for those aged 60-63, automatic enrollment in 401(k) plans for new employees, and relaxed eligibility requirements for part-time employees. Additionally, the Social Security Fairness Act eliminated the Windfall Elimination Provision (WEP) and Government Pension Offset (GPO), impacting those with non-covered pensions.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased catch-up contribution limits for those aged 60-63, automatic enrollment in 401(k) plans for new employees, and relaxed eligibility requirements for part-time employees

text_blocks.snippet: Key Changes from the SECURE 2.0 Act:

list.title: Increased Catch-Up Contributions:
list.snippet: For individuals aged 60-63, the maximum additional catch-up contribution to 401(k) plans increased from $7,500 to $11,250.

list.title: Automatic Enrollment:
list.snippet: New 401(k) plans will require automatic enrollment for eligible employees, with initial contribution rates at a minimum of 3% with annual increases.

list.title: Part-Time Employee Eligibility:
list.snippet: Part-time employees will become eligible for retirement plan participation after two consecutive years of working at least 500 hours.

list.title: Mandatory Roth Catch-Up Contributions:
list.snippet: Starting in 2026, high-earning employees (over $145,000 annually) making catch-up contributions to employer retirement plans will be required to contribute to a Roth account on an after-tax basis.

list.title: Increased 401(k) Contribution Limit:
list.snippet: The annual contribution limit for 401(k), 403(b), 457(b), and Thrift Savings Plan increased to $23,500.

list.title: Increased Catch-Up Contribution Limit for Those 50+:
list.snippet: The catch-up contribution limit for those aged 50 and over also increased to $7,500.

list.title: Increased Catch-Up Contribution Limit for Those 60-63:
list.snippet: If you're between 60-63, your catch-up contribution limit goes up to $11,250.

list.title: Elimination of WEP and GPO:
list.snippet: The Act eliminates the Windfall Elimination Provision (WEP) and Government Pension Offset (GPO), which reduced or eliminated Social Security benefits for those receiving pensions based on non-covered work.

list.title: Increased Benefits:
list.snippet: This change increases Social Security benefits for certain workers, particularly those with non-covered pensions.

list.title: Women's Retirement Protection Act (WRPA):
list.snippet: This act aims to enhance retirement security for women by extending protections and providing tools for better retirement planning.

list.title: Retirement Savings for Americans Act of 2025:
list.snippet: This bill, introduced in the Senate, aims to expand access to retirement savings plans.

list.title: Federal Retirement Fairness Act:
list.snippet: This bill was introduced in the House of Representatives, addressing fairness in federal retirement systems.

text_blocks.snippet: These changes reflect a broader effort to improve retirement savings opportunities and address equity concerns within the retirement system.
